name: kerryback-public
description: Public plugins: a reviewer for work Claude produced, a narrated-video builder for slide decks, a personal literature knowledge base, free financial and economic data, WRDS research data, risk parity portfolios, a shared research repository, an email and calendar desk, and voice whiteboard tutors, and a binomial option pricing tutor that runs in your own Claude Code.

plugins.name: critique
plugins.description: Critique work Claude produced and say what to do about it. Parallel reviewer agents -- correctness traced back to the files that produced each number, clarity, and a devil's advocate that reads the code -- then Claude argues against its own reviewers and publishes an HTML guide that leads with the verdict and lays out the paths forward. Heavyweight: it fans out multiple subagents.

plugins.name: voiceover
plugins.description: Turn a slide deck into a narrated MP4 video plus a transcript. Give it the PDF of your slides and Claude writes the narration; a local app shows each slide beside its script, where you edit it, pick an ElevenLabs voice, and generate. The MP4 and transcript are saved to your working directory.

plugins.name: litdb
plugins.description: Personal literature + notes knowledge base: hybrid keyword+semantic search over your papers and notes, Zotero/Better BibTeX import, loose-PDF folder ingestion with full text, OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar discovery, and a citation graph. Local-first; the runtime installs into ~/.litdb on first use.

plugins.name: finance-data
plugins.description: Fetch free financial, market, and economic data (prices, fundamentals, SEC filings, macro series, asset-pricing factors) from Yahoo, Stooq, SEC EDGAR, FRED, Ken French, FinnHub, FMP, and US Treasury, and save it as CSV.

plugins.name: wrds
plugins.description: Empirical asset-pricing data from WRDS (CRSP v2/Compustat) and Open Source Asset Pricing: extractable Python building blocks for connect (without a 2FA prompt), pull, merge, market cap aggregated across share classes, the CRSP-Compustat link, book equity, accounting alignment and firm age — every query run against live WRDS. Surfaces the constructions that are genuine decisions rather than common practice (Ken French vs Drechsler's WRDS script vs OpenAP, and the 4- vs 6-month reporting lag) instead of picking silently, and ships twelve WRDS reference scripts.

plugins.name: risk-parity
plugins.description: The risk parity (equal risk contribution) portfolio and the covariance matrix it needs, from historical returns, prices, or a covariance matrix: long-only weights in which every asset supplies the same share of portfolio variance, with each asset's risk share and inverse-volatility weight alongside.

plugins.name: research
plugins.description: Set up a research repository several people and their Claudes can share without tripping over each other: per-author folders, portable paths derived rather than configured, one canonical dataset with recorded promotion, provenance read out of the code, project state kept as a directory of one-file-per-entry records so several coauthors write at the same time with no locking and nothing to claim or release, and a generated CLAUDE.md that makes the whole thing self-explaining. Optional two-build (analyst/replicator) protocol for empirical work, an OpenRouter debate panel, and an Overleaf mirror of the paper directory via the git bridge for teams where only some coauthors use Overleaf. Works on a new project or an existing one that grew organically. Ships a vendored writing guide -- economics section formulas and style rules merged with the prose standards that keep drafts from reading as machine-written -- binding for everything in draft/, and it learns: hooks capture the prose corrections you give, /style-learn turns them into rules you accept one at a time and writes them into the guide itself, and the rules your project added are extracted into context at the start of every session. One standard, never a second file of conventions to disagree with it.

plugins.name: smithers
plugins.description: A personal email and calendar desk: your inbox split into what needs a reply, a 7-day calendar with multi-select delete, tasks, and a Compose tab. Claude Code reads your Gmail and Calendar through a local connector, writes a fresh overview of what’s ahead for the next seven days every time the app is opened, and parks drafted replies in Compose — you review and press Send. Sending mail, applying calendar proposals, and editing or deleting events are left to you; the skill's instructions, a hook, and a token in the app's page keep Claude from them.

plugins.name: tutor
plugins.description: Build voice whiteboard tutors for a topic you teach, from your slides, notebooks, or code. A tutor talks, writes on a board, and checks answers with tools. The skill clones the tutor-starter repo, builds the tutor, and stops for your approval at a review page, a local try, evals, and the deploy. Needs an Anthropic API key to run a tutor.

plugins.name: valuation
plugins.description: Two-stage DCF valuation, started with /valuation {ticker}. Runs unattended: fetches statements, 10-Ks, earnings releases and call transcripts from EDGAR and the Motley Fool (set SEC_USER_AGENT to your name and email), makes every judgment call itself and flags each one on the page for review, and builds a tabbed HTML page and an Excel workbook with live formulas. If ~/repos/homepage exists, it also publishes the page there by committing only its own files and pushing.

plugins.name: binomial-tutor
plugins.description: A voice whiteboard tutor for binomial option pricing, run by Claude in your own Claude Code: Claude talks you through one-period, multi-period and American options on a whiteboard in your browser, draws the trees, and checks your answers with exact tools. The voice (Kokoro) and speech recognition (Whisper) are open source and run in the browser, so it needs no API key and no Python packages.
